summary: This Dockerfile creates a Ubuntu container with essential networking tools (jq, curl, certificates) pre-installed. It then seeds the container with a sample JSON file so demonstrations can run without needing to fetch data from the internet, and customizes the shell prompt to show a whale emoji indicating you're inside a container.

explanations.3: This tells Ubuntu's package manager to skip interactive prompts during installation, so the build doesn't hang waiting for user input.
explanations.5: The && chains commands together so if apt-get update fails, the install won't run; rm -rf at the end deletes the package cache to reduce the final image size.
explanations.16: This writes a large JSON string (a fake API response) into a file; the '%s' format tells printf to treat the entire quoted block as a single string without interpreting special characters.
explanations.22: This appends a custom prompt to the bash configuration file; the \e sequences are escape codes that add colors and the whale emoji, and $(whoami) will show the current user name.
explanations.24: This sets the default command to start an interactive bash shell when the container runs, the -i flag makes it behave as if you're logging in interactively.
